verdict.rationale: Fastmail exposes its own token-authenticated JMAP API, so scripts can query, fetch and send mail without the UI, and a community user reports automated transactional sending via SMTP with an SMTP-only app password. There is no official CLI, no CI-specific guidance, and the API-token doc appears only as a title. The JMAP session is runtime discovery rather than a published spec, and the terminal client listed on jmap.io is ecosystem tooling rather than Fastmail's own. missing for 10: official first-party CLI or headless tool, CI/automation-specific documentation, detailed API-token scoping docs, independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
Standard OAuth 2.0 or Bearer tokens. No custom auth protocol to implement.
POST a `methodCalls` array. Query, fetch, and send, all in one HTTP request.
Uses Fastmail SMTP for transactional emails with an app password that can only access SMTP.
